reasons.D: Closest match: long sentences balanced by semicolons and a dash, assertive ironic paradox ('heroic on Monday and shabby on Tuesday, and both from the purest motives'), epigrammatic turns and a crisp worldly close, as in the passage.
reasons.A: Similar period register and semicolon-joined balance with some irony ('I fancy', 'Granted: it is'), but more hedged and even-tempered, with fewer of the passage's sharp paradoxical turns.
reasons.B: Right era and some wit, but chattier and more clubbable ('the other fellow', 'earns its keep'), with shorter conversational sentences and a parenthetical aside that the passage's argumentative stance lacks.
reasons.C: Plain modern expository prose: evenly paced declaratives, explanatory rather than ironic, little semicolon balance and no epigram; furthest from the author's voice.
